text:
alice: Quick QA — after last night's helm upgrade for telemetry-service I started seeing 403s when the pods try to read secrets from the central-credentials namespace. Any chance the serviceaccount selector/labels changed?

ben: ugh. which secret consumer is failing? external-secrets, CSI, or app trying kubernetes API?

alice: external-secrets (kubernetes-external-secrets) backed by the central SecretStore. Error from provider: `permission denied to get secret` in logs. Only started after we bumped telemetry chart to v2.4.0.

carol: can you paste the sa + rolebinding in central-credentials? maybe the RoleBinding was using label selectors and the SA got relabeled.

alice: here are the svcacct + rolebinding snippets from telemetry ns and central-credentials ns:

```
# telemetry namespace
kubectl -n telemetry get sa telemetry -o yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: telemetry
  namespace: telemetry
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: telemetry
    secured-by: team-telemetry
---
# central-credentials namespace
kubectl -n central-credentials get rolebinding credentials-reader -o yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: credentials-reader
  namespace: central-credentials
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: telemetry
  namespace: telemetry
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: read-secrets
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

alice: so it looks like rolebinding uses explicit subject (ns+name). But external-secrets provider is running in telemetry ns and uses a ServiceAccount selector in the SecretStore manifest. I noticed the new chart adds a label `sa-selector: telemetry-v2` to the SA; our SecretStore was selecting `sa-selector: telemetry` so it no longer matches.

ben: ah — so external-secrets uses serviceAccountSelector on the SecretStore/ExternalSecret to decide which pods can request secrets. If the SA label changed, provider won't issue CSR/volume mount and you'll get access denied. Good catch.

carol: can you show the SecretStore/ExternalSecret snippet?

alice: snippet from the SecretStore in telemetry cluster: 
```
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1beta1
kind: SecretStore
metadata:
  name: central-secretstore
  namespace: telemetry
spec:
  provider:
    aws:
      serviceAccountSelector:
        matchLabels:
          sa-selector: telemetry
      role: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/external-secrets-role
```

alice: chart v2.4.0 set SA label to `sa-selector: telemetry-v2` for canary isolation. Helm values defaulted to that and we missed it.

infra-bot: deploy job #2217 finished: telemetry v2.4.0 -> success (:tada:)

ben: options: 1) patch SA labels back to `telemetry` (quick revert), 2) update SecretStore to include both labels (matchExpressions) or accept `telemetry-v2`, 3) change to explicit subject-based RBAC or ClusterRoleBinding for the secret-reader role. For short-term, patch SA label.

carol: agree. patching SA label is fastest. For longer term we should avoid relying solely on labels for cross-namespace secret access — labels are fragile during chart upgrades. Either use explicit subjects in RoleBinding (we already do) or make SecretStore do a matchExpressions with multiple variants.

alice: i'm going to open a tiny patch to the helm values to set `serviceAccount.labels.sa-selector: telemetry` and roll out. I'll also open a follow-up PR to adjust the SecretStore to use `matchExpressions` to allow telemetry and telemetry-v2.

deploy-bot: rollout started: patch/telemetry-sa-label-fix -> telemetry deployment (3 pods)

alice: rolled patch to SA labels and restarted external-secrets pod. After restart the secret is populated and 403s stopped. Thanks for the quick brain dump. :heart:

ben: can we add an infra postmortem note in the chart_upgrade checklist? new item: "verify serviceAccount selector labels if using SecretStore/ExternalSecrets".

carol: also add a quick unit/regression test in our chart repo that asserts SA labels expected by SecretStore values if enabled. I'll add a ticket.

alice: filed perf ticket INFRA-3142 and chart PR 4823 for follow-ups. Marking resolved for now.

infra-bot: incident closed (auto): secret-access-telemetry-1718601234
